definitions: The process by which a sound becomes identical to an adjacent sound.
The full integration of an immigrant or minority group into the dominant culture, losing their original cultural identity.
examples: The complete assimilation of the 'n' sound before 'p' in 'input' is a common phonological change.
Achieving complete assimilation for the new arrivals took several generations.
Linguistic complete assimilation can be observed in many dialects.
